run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: Social Network
Namespace: social-network

A social network with unidirectional follow relationships, implemented with loosely-coupled microservices, communicating with each other via Thrift RPCs.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: Cluster-wide, exactly one workload is failing: Deployment custom-service in namespace social-network has 3/3 replicas unavailable. All 27 other deployments in social-network (compose-post-service, nginx-thrift, user-service, social-graph-service, etc.) report 1 desired / 1 available replica, and a sampled trace of the wrk2 request paths (/wrk2-api/post/compose, /wrk2-api/home-timeline/read, /wrk2-api/user-timeline/read) shows HTTP 200 with the full downstream chain (text, url-shorten, user-mention, social-graph, user-service, media, post-storage, user-timeline, home-timeline) answering in milliseconds, so the social-network request path was not observed failing. The custom-service Deployment was created at 04:09:13 and then patched at 04:09:19 (manager kubectl-patch) to add an init container named hang-init (busybox:1.36, command "/bin/sh -c 'sleep infinity'"). Its rolling strategy is maxSurge 0% / maxUnavailable 100%, so the rollout killed all three previously running pods of ReplicaSet custom-service-5c68f797 and created three new pods (custom-service-6c4f5b6ff6-27mvk, -6v2n5, -77z7r) which are Pending with Initialized=False ("containers with incomplete status: [hang-init]"), init container hang-init running and never ready since 04:09:20, and main container custom-service-main waiting with reason PodInitializing. Root cause: the init container that never exits, held in the custom-service Deployment's pod template. Impact on user-facing social-network traffic is unverified; no Service object named custom-service exists, so nothing in the cluster routes traffic to it in the observed state.

claims.text: Cluster-wide, only Deployment custom-service (namespace social-network) has fewer ready replicas than desired: spec 3, ready=null, available=null, unavailableReplicas=3; all other 42 deployments satisfy ready >= spec.

Deployment custom-service pod template contains init container "hang-init" (image busybox:1.36, command ["/bin/sh","-c","sleep infinity"]) plus main container "custom-service-main" (python:3.9-slim, command python3 -m http.server 8080); the deployment strategy is RollingUpdate with maxSurge 0% and maxUnavailable 100%.

All three custom-service pods (custom-service-6c4f5b6ff6-27mvk on sregym-worker2, -6v2n5 on sregym-worker3, -77z7r on sregym-worker) are phase Pending with PodScheduled=True but Initialized=False reason ContainersNotInitialized message "containers with incomplete status: [hang-init]" and Ready=False reason ContainersNotReady; their init container hang-init is in state running since 04:09:20Z with ready=false and restartCount 0, and container custom-service-main is waiting with reason PodInitializing.

Deployment custom-service was created 2026-11-24T04:09:13Z (manager kubectl-client-side-apply), then updated by manager kubectl-patch at 04:09:19Z and kubectl-rollout at 04:09:20Z, reaching generation 3 with observedGeneration 3 and status.replicas 3 / updatedReplicas 3 / unavailableReplicas 3.

Namespace social-network events show the custom-service rollout: ReplicaSet custom-service-5c68f797 pods custom-service-5c68f797-5dbj2/-7g8v6/-qksjr were Stopping/Killing and Deleted at 04:09:19-04:09:20 while Deployment custom-service "Scaled down replica set custom-service-5c68f797 from 3 to 0" and "Scaled up replica set custom-service-6c4f5b6ff6 from 0 to 3" at 04:09:20, and the new pods' hang-init containers were Created and Started at 04:09:20Z.

No Service object named custom-service exists in namespace social-network: the 30 Services and 26 Endpoints listed for the namespace contain only the social-network application services (compose-post-service, nginx-thrift, user-service, ... ) and the jaeger ExternalName entries.

Every social-network application deployment other than custom-service reported available=ready=1 with replicas=1 at query time (e.g. compose-post-service, home-timeline-service, media-service, nginx-thrift, post-storage-service, social-graph-service, text-service, unique-id-service, url-shorten-service, user-service, user-mention-service, user-timeline-service).

Sampled traces of the social-network request path at 04:09:22-04:09:35Z show nginx-web-server spans /wrk2-api/post/compose, /wrk2-api/home-timeline/read and /wrk2-api/user-timeline/read with http.status_code=200 (7.6 ms max in the sample), with child spans on compose-post-service, text-service, url-shorten-service, user-mention-service, social-graph-service, user-service, media-service, unique-id-service, post-storage-service, user-timeline-service and home-timeline-service and no error rows in the shown spans.

compose-post-service pod compose-post-service-659bfc5898-cbqjp logged only "Starting the compose-post-service server ..." at 04:09:05.561Z in its current container stream (no previous container instance), i.e. no error lines were returned for it.

Startup-time noise was present in other services: post-storage-service, user-service, user-timeline-service and url-shorten-service logged "Failed to create mongodb index" with "No suitable servers found: serverSelectionTimeoutMS expired" between 04:09:05Z and 04:09:08Z, and FailedMount warnings for configmap volumes (post-storage-service-config, user-mongodb-config) occurred at 04:09:05Z.

Those services that logged MongoDB index-creation and mount errors at startup were Running and Ready (1/1 available) later in the window, and the traced requests they participate in returned HTTP 200, so those startup errors were not accompanied by observed failures in the sampled data.

Insufficient node capacity or unschedulable pods did not cause the custom-service pods to stay Pending: all three pods have PodScheduled=True and were assigned to three different nodes (sregym-worker, sregym-worker2, sregym-worker3), and no FailedScheduling event exists in the namespace event set.

Image pull failure or container crash did not block custom-service: the hang-init image (busybox:1.36) was already present and the hang-init container is running (not waiting or terminated), the pod shows restartCount 0 and no back-off or crashloop state.

Because the custom-service template has no readiness probe and maxUnavailable 100% with maxSurge 0%, any rollout whose init step does not finish takes all replicas down at once; a probe plus maxUnavailable < 100% would have limited the blast radius. This is an inference about the rollout mechanics, not an observed additional fault.

Remove the never-terminating hang-init init container from Deployment custom-service (or roll the deployment back to the revision before the 04:09:19Z patch) so custom-service-main can start, then confirm all 3 replicas reach Ready; additionally consider a readiness probe on port 8080 and a rolling strategy that does not allow 100% unavailability.

gaps: Author and intent of the change could not be verified: the change_history integration is not integrated, so it is unknown who/what issued the kubectl-patch at 04:09:19Z that added init container hang-init to Deployment custom-service; only the managedFieldsSummary last-write time and the rollout events were observable.

The observability data begins with the namespace itself: namespace objects were created at 04:09:03-04:09:13Z and the oldest social-network Loki lines returned were 04:09:05Z, so there is no baseline covering the earlier part of the authorized window and no comparison of custom-service before/after the patch beyond the events.

Trace evidence comes only from traces_search_by_tags biased samples (5 traces, 04:09:22-04:09:35Z, and 5 traces at 04:09:32-04:09:35Z); the non-tag traces_search tool rejected social-network service names with INVALID_PARAMS, so a complete call graph, error rate and latency distribution for the app could not be established.

No error-rate/latency metric series were returned for the app: get_series for traces_span_metrics_calls_total returned no series and increase(traces_span_metrics_calls_total[...]) returned no data, so absence of app errors is inferred only from the sampled traces, not from a full error-rate metric.

Whether custom-service is supposed to serve any application traffic is unknown: no Service or Endpoints object named custom-service exists and the template has no readiness probe, so the user-facing consequence of its 3/3 unavailability is unverified.
Events were the only evidence for when the init container was introduced and for the rollout sequence; object state at query time cannot prove what the deployment looked like earlier in the window.
next_steps: Review the custom-service Deployment revision history and the kubectl patch applied at 2026-11-24T04:09:19Z to confirm the hang-init init container was introduced deliberately by the change that triggered the failed rollout.
After the fix, verify custom-service pods move past PodInitializing to Running/Ready and that Deployment custom-service reports 3/3 available replicas.
Determine whether custom-service is expected to be reachable (Service/readiness probe) so that its availability can be monitored rather than inferred from pod phase.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.
